caption: Diagram 3.4
description: A floor plan of a flat with an alternative exit, where the habitable rooms don't all have direct access to an entrance hall (see para 3.19). The 'Flat entrance' at the bottom opens into a large 'Living room', and the 'Kitchen' opens off the living room on the right. A fire doorset ('Fd') leads from the living room into a small inner hall serving a 'Bedroom' at the top left, a 'Bedroom' at the top right, a 'Bedroom' at the middle left and a 'Bath' at the middle right. A green line between the living room and the bedrooms is 'Fire resisting construction (minimum REI 30) between living and bedroom accommodation'. The top right-hand bedroom has a door to an 'Alternative exit', shown by a green arrow. A thick black line marks compartment walls: 'See Appendix B for fire resistance of compartment walls separating a flat from any other part of the building or other occupancies'. NOTE: 'The bedrooms are not classified as inner rooms because escape is possible in two directions.'
model_description:
This diagram is a floor plan for a flat with an alternative exit. The plan shows a layout including a living room, kitchen, bath, and three bedrooms. The flat entrance is located at the bottom of the plan, leading into the living room. A hallway connects the living room to the kitchen, bath, and bedrooms. One bedroom is located in the top left, another in the top middle, and a third in the top right. The alternative exit is indicated by a green arrow pointing out of a door in the top right bedroom.

A symbol labelled 'Fd' refers to a fire doorset located between the living room and the hallway. A green line indicates fire resisting construction (minimum REI 30) between living and bedroom accommodation. A black rectangle represents compartment walls; a note states to see Appendix B for the fire resistance of compartment walls separating a flat from any other part of the building or other occupancies. A note also states: "The bedrooms are not classified as inner rooms because escape is possible in two directions."
